items.item_text: resume

The VCR serves as UC Berkeley’s senior executive leader for research policy, planning, and administration, leading the research division and partnering with faculty, deans, and other campus leaders to advance the University’s broader research mission. The VCR provides strategic and administrative leadership for the research enterprise and executive oversight of the research administration, integrity, compliance, and support functions that enable research across the Berkeley campus.
Strategic Vision & Research Excellence:
Partner with the Chancellor, EVCP, deans, and faculty to help ensure the continued excellence of Berkeley’s research mission in an ever-evolving research environment.

Catalyze interdisciplinary and cross-campus research initiatives, bringing together faculty, schools, colleges, research units, and external partners around emerging opportunities and areas of strategic importance to Berkeley.
Help the campus anticipate changes in the research landscape and develop new approaches to research funding, partnerships, infrastructure, and institutional support.
Enhance the value of Berkeley research for private industry (technology licensing, startup companies, and industry partnership), public policy, and direct engagement with communities.

Advance the visibility of Berkeley’s research enterprise, partnering with campus communications, academic leaders, and other stakeholders to elevate faculty scholarship, research accomplishments, and Berkeley’s contributions to society.
Serve as a spokesperson for Berkeley research.
Organizational Leadership & Management:

Provide strategic oversight of over 100 interdisciplinary research institutes, centers, museums, field stations, research support units, shared user facilities and other organizations reporting to the VCR, ensuring strong leadership, effective stewardship of resources, strong engagement of campus faculty and researchers, and alignment with campus research priorities.

Lead efforts to modernize and streamline research administration, reducing inefficient administrative burden and improving the systems, processes, and services that enable faculty and researchers to conduct research effectively.

Lead and support organizational change, systems transformation, and process improvement across the research enterprise, working with campus partners to develop more effective and flexible ways of operating.

Maintain a strong leadership team and delegate effectively so that the VCR can maintain strategic focus while ensuring the organization has the capacity to manage its substantial operational and compliance responsibilities.
Research Administration, Integrity & Compliance:

Provide executive oversight of the infrastructure, policies, services, and compliance functions that support Berkeley’s research enterprise, including sponsored research administration, research integrity, human and animal research protections, research security, export controls, conflicts of interest, environment, health and safety, and other areas of regulatory compliance.

Ensure that Berkeley maintains the highest standards of research integrity and that campus research complies with applicable federal, state, University, and institutional policies and regulations, while promoting processes that enable and support the research mission.

Strengthen Berkeley’s ability to attract, secure, and effectively administer external research funding, working with faculty, research administrators, government agencies, foundations, industry, and other partners.

Provide strategic leadership for the entrepreneurship ecosystem, intellectual property, technology transfer, industry research relationships, and other mechanisms that broaden the reach and impact of Berkeley research.

Provide leadership on campus research policy and ensure that policies and practices appropriately balance research opportunity, institutional risk, regulatory requirements, and the needs of faculty and researchers.
Campus Governance & Collaboration:
Serve on the Chancellor's Cabinet and the Provost’s Council, among other campus leadership groups.
Act as a principal liaison to the campus’s Academic Senate on research matters.
Navigate Berkeley’s decentralized, shared-governance environment and build alignment across faculty, staff, deans, campus leaders, and other stakeholders.

Partner closely with deans and other academic leaders to support research across Berkeley’s schools, colleges, and divisions, serving as a catalyst and partner in shaping research strategy rather than its sole owner.
Foster close cooperative relationships with academic deans to support research conducted across Berkeley’s schools, colleges, and divisions.

Represent the Chancellor or EVCP, as appropriate, on campus committees and initiatives addressing research-related infrastructure, fundraising, budget, policy, and other matters affecting Berkeley’s research enterprise.
System-wide & National Representation:

Represent Berkeley on the UC Council of Vice Chancellors for Research; the APLU Committee on Research; and the AAU Senior Research Officer groups, and in other organizations involving university research leaders.

Anticipate and respond to changes in the federal research funding and policy environment and work with UC system leadership, federal and state agencies, and policymakers to advocate for Berkeley’s research enterprise and position the campus for emerging opportunities.
Collaborate with other UC VCRs to manage multi-campus research units, initiatives, and programs.
Internal Administrative Partnerships:

Work with the Vice Provost for the Faculty and academic leaders on the recruitment and retention of an outstanding and diverse community of faculty researchers; collaborate with the Chief Information Officer on strategic computing, security, and infrastructure; partner with the Vice Chancellor for Administration to oversee Environment, Health and Safety; and coordinate with the Vice Chancellors for Administration and Finance on facilities investments, administrative services supporting research, and other key funding considerations.

Partner with academic deans, the Vice Chancellor for Administration, and Vice Provost for Academic Planning to advocate for, and raise funds for updating and renewal of research infrastructure (buildings, facilities), shared user facilities, and other core infrastructure (IT network, supply chain, etc) to enable cutting edge research across campus.

Assess and strengthen shared research facilities, core infrastructure, museums, field stations, and other research “common goods,” including the development of sustainable operating and financial models.

Help to manage the close research partnership and administrative interface with the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL), University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) and the partnership with NASA Ames.

Strengthen relationships with federal agencies, industry, foundations, national laboratories, and other external partners to diversify and expand research opportunities while balancing institutional priorities, financial considerations, risk, and research integrity.

Support the broad dissemination and visibility of Berkeley’s research and scholarship through external engagement and other avenues that extend the reach and societal impact of the University’s research enterprise.
Key Opportunities and Challenges

The role is multifaceted as an inspiring intellectual leader who champions diverse research activities, facilitates cross-disciplinary innovation, and acts as an operational change agent capable of effecting positive, significant change in infrastructure and organizational structures.
Funding Diversification & External Advocacy
Navigating Federal Volatility:
Understanding, communicating, and leading the navigation of shifting federal agency priorities, grant disruptions, and heightened regulatory mandates (research security, export controls).
Alternative Funding Streams:

The next VCR may proactively build and leverage relationships to diversify funding streams, maintaining connections with federal agencies while pursuing opportunities from industry partnerships, private philanthropy, and foundations.
Facilitating Broad Collaborations:
Capitalize on California state funding, cross-UC collaborations, or interdisciplinary initiatives on campus in high-impact areas.
Change Leadership on Infrastructure & Organizational Structures for Research Administration
Change Management for Research Administration:

Collaborate with campus leaders and administration to reduce administrative burden and overall RA process complications for faculty and researchers. Address and communicate effective process and systems improvements.
Strategy for Shared Facilities:
Evaluate and build sustainable financial models to operate, upgrade, and recapitalize shared core facilities and specialized units.
Future-Proofing Buildings & Spaces:
Collaboratively address deferred facilities maintenance and space constraints that hinder research growth.
Systems & Technology Solutions:
Partner with the Finance and IT leadership to modernize aging enterprise systems and safely integrate emerging AI tools where appropriate and relevant.
Intellectual Leadership, Research Vision, & Values-Based Leadership
Champion the Research Enterprise:
Ensuring humanities, social sciences, and STEM all receive strategic support.
Catalyze large-scale interdisciplinary initiatives without creating additional administrative silos. Advance innovation and entrepreneurship while supporting fundamental research.
Decisive and Principled Approach:

Exercise a principled and ethical compass, bring an aspirational vision for research support and strategy at Berkeley, and maintain the willingness and consistency to make and communicate complex/difficult decisions based on aligned values and vision.
Diverse Stakeholders Communication:
Communicate with clarity, empathy, and composure during crises, regulatory disruptions, and moments of institutional uncertainty.
The Forest and The Trees:
Balance high-level strategic vision with a realistic, grounded understanding of day-to-day administrative operations.
Connecting with Institutional Equity
: Preserve and communicate Berkeley's research success in service of its public mission, societal impact, and commitment to institutional equity.
Faculty Partner & Liaison:

Listen and leverage connections, and resolve and/or elevate issues of concern among the faculty to campus leadership; serve as an advocate for faculty and researchers. Convey direction, alignment, and relevant issues and trends of concern to faculty relating to research.
Navigating UC Berkeley and Managing Complexity
Shared Governance & Decentralization:
Understand and effectively navigate Berkeley’s decentralized ecosystem, being part of a state system, and shared governance model, relying on coalition-building and influence for success.

Navigate labor dynamics effectively, adapting to student, and postdoc unionization that has transformed mentor-mentee dynamics into formal employment frameworks. Navigate unionization of research support staff.
Visionary Management & Delegation:

Provide calm and motivational leadership to a large and complex division while maintaining a culture of service orientation. Delegate operational tasks effectively to a trusted senior team to manage a massive portfolio encompassing ~2,300 personnel and multi-layered compliance duties.
Organized Research Units:
Provide clear oversight of Organized Research Units (ORUs), focusing on strategic alignment, cross-disciplinary growth, and sustainable financial models.

The challenges/opportunities and priorities for the VCR are multi-directional, and the research ecosystem and federal landscape are ever-changing. The next VCR will need to be strongly grounded in their vision for the research enterprise at Berkeley and core values so that they may strategically lead their team, collaborate, influence, and drive change in support of researchers.
Qualifications and Characteristics

The ideal candidate will be a distinguished scholar and researcher with strong skills in leadership, administration, collaboration, and communication who can bring and advance a vision for research at UC Berkeley that aligns with the mission and culture of Berkeley, its executive leadership, and the campus community.
A distinguished record of excellence in research, teaching, and/or professional activity appropriate for a tenured faculty appointment in one or more of UC Berkeley’s academic departments.
University of California (UC) Expertise:
Current or recent UC experience is strongly preferred to support learning agility in navigating organizational and role complexities.

Excellent skills to think strategically and establish a vision and roadmap for research at Berkeley that is aligned with campus executives, researchers, and the community. Excellent ability to advance initiatives and understand details while maintaining clarity on big picture shared goals.
Administrative Leadership:
Demonstrated success in managing a complex unit, organization, team, and/or lab.
Strong skills to lead significant organizational change, transformation, restructuring, or enterprise-level implementation in a complex institution.
Leading Through Influence:

Demonstrated ability to lead effectively in a complex, decentralized, shared-governance environment; build alignment across diverse stakeholders; and influence outcomes without relying primarily on positional authority.
Team Leadership & Delegation:

Excellent skills to build and develop high-performing leadership teams, delegate effectively, mentor and coach others, provide thought partnership, motivate towards common goals, and hold accountability.
Fundraising & Funding Success:

Proven ability to secure major research funding; strong skills to support programs outside their direct domain of expertise and serve as an effective fundraiser with alumni, industry, and governmental stakeholders. Experienced in navigating multiple funding models and balancing financial opportunity with institutional priorities, risk, research integrity, and long-term sustainability.

Strong financial acumen with a record of transparency and accountability in resource management. Ability to understand the financial and operational implications of research infrastructure, shared facilities, indirect cost recovery, and evolving research funding models.
Systems Thinking and Process Improvement:

Strong ability for deep analysis and build understanding of the systems and administrative infrastructure that underpin a major research enterprise, with the ability to identify barriers, improve processes, problem solve, and translate and communicate complex operational, technological, financial, and regulatory issues into practical solutions for researchers and staff.

Deep understanding of the legislative, regulatory, public policy, and compliance environments impacting higher education research. Demonstrated ability to navigate research security, export controls, international research requirements, data and privacy considerations, intellectual property, and rapidly evolving regulatory environments.
Intellectual Leadership & Curiosity Across Disciplines:

Demonstrated intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage credibly across disciplines, appreciate different research methods and perspectives, and advance work beyond traditional academic or organizational silos. Desire for engagement with the full breadth of an institution’s academic and research enterprise, including disciplines and communities beyond the candidate’s primary field of expertise.
Commitment to Institutional Values:
Demonstrated history of implementing successful strategies and programs that attract, support, and retain students, faculty, and staff from diverse backgrounds.
Values-Driven Leadership:

The position requires the highest personal integrity, a clear sense of self, and principled, values-based grounding aligned with the campus vision and community. A calm, steady leadership presence and the confidence to help faculty, staff, and campus partners remain focused and grounded during periods of significant change or crisis.
Communication & Political Acumen:

Exceptional skills in listening, writing, and presenting to diverse internal and external audiences. Exceptional political judgment, diplomacy, and interpersonal skill, including the ability to understand different stakeholder perspectives, tailor messages to different audiences, de-escalate conflict, and maintain trust during periods of uncertainty or disagreement.
Ethics & Decision Making:

A strong moral compass and the courage to make, explain, and stand behind difficult or unpopular decisions, including decisions involving funding, partnerships, compliance, research security, and institutional priorities, while maintaining respectful and productive relationships.

Confidence tempered by humility, including a willingness to listen to experts, acknowledge what one does not know, seek advice when appropriate, learn quickly, and adapt leadership approaches as circumstances evolve.

Experience engaging with federal agencies, government, industry, foundations, national laboratories, or other external research partners is highly desirable, as is an understanding of the broader national and international research landscape.
Inquiries, Nominations, and Applications

The review of applications will begin on September 29, 2026. For full consideration, those interested should apply by September 29, 2026 at noon PT. The position will remain open until filled. All those interested in applying for official consideration are asked to do so via
. Candidates should submit both a CV/resume and a letter of interest.
All inquiries and nominations should be directed to the university’s internal executive search partner, the Berkeley Executive Search team at
executivesearch+vcr@berkeley.edu

pay.source_text: The anticipated annual range that the University reasonably expects to offer is $500,000 to $560,000. The estimated pay scale for the role and classification ranges from $460,000 to $580,000.
